MINUTES

  SPECIAL MEETING
  GLENDALE TRANSPORTATION & PARKING COMMISSION
  March 4, 2019

The regular meeting of the Glendale Transportation & Parking Commission (TPC) of Monday,
March 4, 2019 was called to order at 6:00 p.m.

1. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA – 6:00 p.m. Chairperson Kurkjian called the meeting to
  order.
  a. Roll Call –Gonzalez, Yacoubian, Chairperson Kurkjian, Sahakian, Nazarian
  b. Flag Salute – Chairperson Kurkjian

2. POSTING OF AGENDA
  The agenda for the Monday, March 4, 2019 Regular Meeting of the Glendale
  Transportation & Parking Commission was posted by Friday, March 1, 2019 before 5:00
  p.m. on the bulletin board outside of City Hall.

3. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items NOT a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five
  minutes. The Commission may question the speaker but there will be no debate or
  decision.
  There were no speakers at this time.

4. INFORMATION ONLY
  a. North Hollywood to Pasadena Bus Rapid Transit Update

Scott Hartwell from Metro presented on various aspects of the North Hollywood to Pasadena Bus
Rapid Transit (BRT) studies recently conducted. He explained that they would have access to
$267 million to fund this project. The project is expected to begin between the Fiscal Year 2022
and 2024. Metro had found that frequency, connectivity and convenience to be the three main
priorities of potential riders of the proposed BRT. The BRT seemed to gain broad support from the
residents of Glendale, where people mentioned they preferred a street operated bus, rather than a
freeway path for the BRT. Daily ridership was reportedly expected to be around 30,000 people.
Mr. Hartwell then went on to discuss some of the benefits of the BRT such as its significantly lower
cost compared to light rail and the fact that the buses would be eco-friendly resulting in less air and
noise pollution. Mr. Hartwell discussed Metro’s next steps after completing the conceptual
engineering aspect of the project, they would be ready to present to the Metro Board by April 2019.
Commissioner Gonzalez asked how the Metro’s design would work if the BRT and the street car
occupy the same stops along the streets and which would work better, having them together or
having them operate on separate streets.

Mr. Terry Nash from the City’s consulting firm, HNTB Corporation, replied that they are not that far
along in their study. They plan to work with Metro to figure out where stations would be.
Commissioner Gonzalez asked if there are plans to extend the bus path father up north above the
134 freeway and Mr. Nash explained they will continue to work with the City in the study.
Mr. Hartwell said BRT will be the first to be implemented and would commence service in the year
2024. The BRT is fully funded and is very flexible because it has no track to build.
Commissioner Gonzalez asked if there expects to be any impact on the stops for the street car.
Mr. Hartwell explained that the situation may vary, but they do anticipate to share stops with the
street cars as well as shade structures and digital display signs located at the stops.

  Page 1 of 2
 Commissioner Yacoubian asked since the main purpose of the BRT is to provide public
transportation for residents coming and going to Bob Hope Airport, will the BRT be capable of
holding luggage. Mr. Hartwell said unlike the FlyAway bus operated out of union station, the BRT
buses will not have that capability or the space.
Commissioner Sahakian expressed his concerns regarding the already heavily congested area
along both Brand Boulevard and Central Avenue as well as along Colorado Boulevard and
Broadway. He added that it would not be advisable to take away a travel lane when there is little
space as it is. He urged Metro to take a look at other Cities utilizing various forms of new
technology to transport people, rather than using buses.
Commissioner Nazarian asked if there were any plans for right of way acquisitions and Mr. Hartwell
replied that they planned on operating on City streets alone.
Chairperson Kurkjian asked if in the engineers who have designed the large setbacks for the
shade structures have considered the buildings and property that already occupy that area. Mr.
Hartwell mentioned they are still looking at studies pertaining to this issue.
Commissioner Gonzalez asked if the City was going to ask the Commission for any
recommendation considering the BRT. Mr. Edward Hitti mentioned there would not be any need
for further action from the Commission.

5. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS/UPDATES

Commissioner Yacoubian asked Mr. Hitti for an update on the right turning lane by the 2 freeway
onramp on Mountain Avenue that had been discussed in the previous meeting. Mr. Hitti assured
Commissioner Yacoubian that there will be an update provided by the next Transportation and
Parking Commission meeting on March 25, 2019.
Chairperson Kurkjian introduced the newest Commissioner of the TPC, Commissioner Henrik
Nazarian.

6. ADJOURNMENT: 6:40 p.m.

Moved: Sahakian  Second: Gonzalez
